Public Portion 
 1. Proposed ordinance to ban crypto kiosks in the City of Springfield. 
On November 12, 2026, the Public Safety Committee, chaired by Councilor Gerry Martin, met to 
review a proposed ordinance prohibiting virtual currency kiosks in the City of Springfield. 
Representatives from the Springfield Police Department reported approximately $1.4 million in 
cryptocurrency-related fraud losses, with many incidents involving kiosks located in 
convenience stores and gas stations. Police officials described scams targeting residents of 
various ages, difficulties recovering transferred funds, and investigative challenges involving 
cryptocurrency transactions and individuals operating outside the United States. 
 
The committee reviewed the proposed ordinance developed by the Mayor's Administration and 
Law Department. Attorney Cohen explained that the ordinance uses broad definitions of virtual 
currency kiosks and electronic terminals to address different types of transactions and prevent 
circumvention of the regulations. Under the proposal, affected kiosks would become inoperable 
immediately upon the ordinance taking effect and would be required to be physically removed 
within 15 days. Discussion also addressed the limitations of existing enforcement measures and 
the importance of preventing financial fraud. The proposed requirements were presented for 
consideration and had not yet been adopted. 
 
A motion was made and seconded to advance the proposed ordinance to the full City Council. 
The meeting adjourned at 1:26 p.m.
